participant_crosswalk.rule: Princeton sN maps to transcript NNxx with the same integer N
participant_crosswalk.source: Table 1, Word-timestamped transcripts of two spoken narrative recall functional neuroimaging datasets

splits.method: sha256 rank of cmwm-sherlock-v1:sN, frozen before retrieval

fine_units.grouping: one record per released fine-grained label row

random_matched.grouping: oracle event-length multiset shuffled across the same atomic sequence

evaluation.query_unit: one aggregated text query per recalled participant-scene pair
evaluation.overlap_diagnostic_target: any retrieved record containing at least one atomic unit from the coded scene
evaluation.single_target: the deterministic record with maximum atomic-segment IoU to the coded human scene
evaluation.graded_relevance: atomic-segment IoU between each record and the coded human scene
evaluation.primary_metric: participant-macro hit@5 for the single maximum-IoU target record
evaluation.revision_reason: v1 overlap hit rewarded boundary-crossing conditions with multiple relevant records per query

limitations: Post-v1 development metric correction; no held-out test access and no confirmatory claim.

The released label sequence contains one zero-duration row and one timestamp reset between its two source parts; both are retained and audited because retrieval uses sequence order rather than duration.

Encoding records use scene markers in the released 1,000-label file, whereas recall targets use the primary 50-scene annotation; corresponding boundaries are one-to-one but can differ by up to three seconds.
BM25 record length and sparse-index cost are not byte matched across segmentation conditions.
The maximum-IoU single target is a deterministic evaluation construct; IoU-nDCG is reported to avoid relying on it alone.
Dense fixed-width embeddings are required before a matched-memory claim.
No causal graph or fMRI is used.
